title: Exchange Wands
description: Exchange Wands is a lightweight, polished vanilla+ utility mod that lets you swap blocks in the world with ease.
body:
![Title](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/14b3ab13322a271273aca2f3c7cb007ef3ad8ac1.png)

## ✨ Features
### 🔍 Select Any Block
Sneak + RMB a block to set it as your _source block_.
The wand remembers your selection and shows a clean actionbar message.
### 🔄 Replace Blocks with Flood‑Fill Logic
RMB a block to replace all connected blocks of the same type.
The wand uses a safe, optimized flood‑fill algorithm that respects:
- block properties (facing, waterlogged, lit…)
- inventories (chests, barrels, furnaces…)
- NBT data (restored when compatible)
- tile entity transfers
- survival inventory limits
- durability and cooldowns
### 🎨 Property‑Preserving Replacement
Exchange Wands copy all shared blockstate properties automatically.
Orientation, waterlogging, lit state, slab halves - everything transfers seamlessly.
### 📦 Inventory‑Aware
In survival mode:
- the wand only replaces blocks you have
- it removes one item per exchange
- it drops overflow items safely
### 🔧 Fully Configurable
- maximum exchange size
- bedrock protection
- sound & particle toggles
### 💎 Vanilla Tool Tiers

## 🎵 Polished Player Feedback
Exchange Wands include:
- selection sounds
- exchange sounds
- block‑themed placement/break audio
- particle effects for selection and replacement
All effects can be toggled in the config.

## 🧩 Compatibility
Exchange Wands work with:
- all vanilla blocks
- modded blocks that follow standard blockstate rules
- inventories and tile entities

## 📦 Lightweight & Server‑Friendly
No mixins that modify vanilla behavior.
No worldgen.
No performance impact.

Just clean, deterministic block replacement.

## 🛠️ Perfect for Builders
Whether you are:
- upgrading your base
- replacing floors
- fixing walls
- terraforming
- or building megastructures

Exchange Wands make block replacement effortless.

_This mod was originally developed for Minecraft 1.20.1. I am gradually migrating it to newer versions, ensuring each update is stable, polished, and fully adapted to the latest APIs._
